trial_court: Family Court, Bemetara (Civil Case No.21A/2015 and Civil Suit No.1-A/2016)
case_name: Smt. Richa Mishra vs Navodit Mishra
facts_of_case: The parties were married under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The wife filed an application for restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of the Act, which was dismissed by the trial court. The husband also filed an application for a decree of divorce under Section 13(1)(i-a), (i-b) and (iii) of the Act, which was also dismissed. Both parties appealed to this court.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the applicant to prove that the respondent has wilfully neglected or refused to perform his/her conjugal obligations.
legal_principles.held: It is held that the burden lies on the applicant to prove that the respondent has wilfully neglected or refused to perform his/her conjugal obligations.

legal_principles.principle: The court will not grant a decree for restitution of conjugal rights unless the applicant has made out a prima facie case.
legal_principles.held: It is held that the court will not grant a decree for restitution of conjugal rights unless the applicant has made out a prima facie case.

outcome.final_order: The appeal filed by the wife was dismissed, and a decree of divorce was granted in favour of the husband under Section 13(1)(i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
